extracted.intended_audience: Academic researchers, principal investigators, and multi-university teams preparing FY25 MURI white papers and proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare multi-university research proposals (white papers and full proposals) responding to specific FY25 MURI topic descriptions, meeting topic objectives, suggested research concentration areas, team composition, and resource constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Quantum simulators for materials properties
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of this MURI is to study materials properties at the microscopic level using quantum simulator platforms and model systems implemented on them to gain new fundamental insights into the mechanical, thermal, and/or vibrational behavior of materials. A secondary objective is to use quantum simulator platforms to accelerate the iterative process of identifying and designing new materials with physical properties of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particular interest in explorations beyond purely electronic, spintronic, optoelectronic, and photonic behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — theoretical approaches to design materials
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) theoretical approaches (computational and analytical) to design real or model materials
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes computational and analytical theory to design materials or models amenable to quantum simulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — experimental quantum simulation techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) experimental quantum simulation techniques and platforms to explore materials properties and behavior
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should include experimental platforms and techniques for implementing model systems on quantum simulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — theoretical tools for extracting properties
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) theoretical tools for understanding and extracting the materials properties from quantum simulations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes methods for mapping simulator outputs to physical material properties and interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — materials fabrication and benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) materials fabrication and characterization techniques for benchmarking simulation results and realizing new materials designs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should include fabrication and characterization to benchmark and validate quantum simulation results against conventional experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — incorporate simulator insights into computational techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: (5) incorporating insights and data from quantum simulators into computational materials science techniques to improve fidelity, functionality, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals may describe how simulator-derived data can improve or augment hybrid density functional theory, molecular dynamics, or other computational methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — funding and team size (quantum simulators)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than an average of $1.5M per year for up to 5 years, supporting no more than 6 funded faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions should be discussed with topic chiefs during the white paper phase as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Fundamental limits of distributed entangled quantum sensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore the fundamental and practical limits in sensing with a distributed entangled sensor network, including analysis of quantum state type, network topology and signal processing approach needed to reach limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider continuous, discrete, and hybrid variable states, resilience to loss and decoherence, and resource accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — novel modalities for distributed entanglement
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Novel modalities for the use of distributed entanglement in continuous, discrete and hybrid variable states in a network of sensors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate modalities beyond squeezing and single-apparatus demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — study fundamental limits of distributed sensing
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) Study of the fundamental limits of performance of a distributed entangled sensing network (e.g. Is there any advantage beyond the known Heisenberg-scale sensitivity? Can quantum resources other than entanglement (e.g. non-locality) be leveraged?)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes information theoretic analyses and comparisons to known limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — network topologies and characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) Analysis of advantages and challenges of different network topologies and characteristics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how topology impacts performance, resilience, and resource requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — signal processing for distributed sensors
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) Exploration of signal processing techniques needed to combine the signals from the different sensors (including how to combine signals from disparate sensors and make the system resilient to node corruption).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes development and evaluation of algorithms to fuse disparate sensor data and handle corrupted nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — funding and team size (Topic 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than an average of $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than 5 funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chief during the white paper phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: HBCU/MI participation incentive (Topic 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for Topic 17 are invited that include participation from eligible HBCUs/MIs; applications with an HBCU/MI MURI team member may be eligible for $1.5M in total additional funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HBCU/MI participation is not a requirement but may provide additional funding eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Foundation Models for Perception
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop architectures for understanding complex, dynamic environments from multi-modal data, with emphasis on inferring activities and causal models; investigate how to exploit Foundation Models (FMs) for perception inverse problems and develop rigorous evaluation methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address FM shortcomings (incorrect responses, logical inconsistencies, inadequate inference) and investigate representation, grounding, and mathematical performance prediction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — principled architectures for FMs
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Investigate and design principled architectures and computational methods for incorporating Foundation Models (FMs) for solving the inverse problem of perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on architectures that use FMs for multi-modal perception tasks like activities and causality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — methods to handle FM inaccuracies
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) Develop rigorous methods to deal with inaccurate information that FMs may generate, and methods for detecting their potential internal logical inconsistencies and how to prevent and correct them. Also, investigate methods for improving the inference capabilities of FMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detection, correction, and methods to make FMs reliably safe for critical applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — distillation and deployment of FMs
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) Investigate how the information contained in FMs can be distilled for particular application scenarios, and how FMs can be reduced for deployment on small mobile platforms and what the performance loss may be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include techniques for model compression, distillation, and evaluation of trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — mathematical performance prediction
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) Develop rigorous mathematical methods to predict the performance of perception systems that incorporate FMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical methods should reduce reliance on purely empirical evaluation, especially for corner cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — funding and team size (Topic 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than an average of $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting at most 8 funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with topic chiefs during the white paper phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Ionosphere impacts from tropospheric gravity waves
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a quantitative numerical representation of lower atmosphere gravity wave coupling through mesospheric-ionospheric fate modeling that is underpinned by theoretical models while matching observationally based empirical models to improve prediction of ionospheric structure beyond diurnal solar forcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires multidisciplinary collaboration among atmospheric scientists, physicists, observational and numerical experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — sources & climatology identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Science should focus on (1) Identification and characterization of sources, occurrences, and climatology of non-orographic tropospheric gravity wave generation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include observational and diagnostic studies to characterize generation mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — gravity wave propagation mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Science should focus on (2) Mechanics of neutral atmosphere gravity wave propagation, coupling into the mesosphere and evolution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address propagation, breaking, dissipation and coupling processes through modeling and theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — effects on charged particle distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Science should focus on (3) Sensible effects of gravity waves on charged particle distribution and evolution in the ionosphere
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include impacts on ionospheric structure, dynamics, chemistry, photo-ionization and recombination relevant to DoD operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — funding and team size (Topic 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards under this topic will be no more than $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than five funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may be discussed during the white paper phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Coastal processes & permafrost erosion
rubrics_metrics.description: Support a multidisciplinary team to create and validate through observations a comprehensive coastal erosion model for permafrost systems, accounting for spatial and temporal variability, thermoerosional & block failure mechanisms, submarine permafrost, and effects of sediment and carbon inputs on the shelf environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize validation with observations and modeling of thermal-mechanical permafrost erosion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — state-of-the-art coastal ocean model/module
rubrics_metrics.description: Research teams must incorporate the expertise needed for creation of a state-of-the-art, comprehensive coastal ocean model/module for thermal-mechanical permafrost erosion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams must include expertise in coastal wave modeling and permafrost erosion; additional suggested areas include Arctic oceanography & meteorology, sea ice dynamics, cryohydrogeology & geomorphology, and coastal remote sensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — funding and team size (Topic 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than an average of $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than five (5) funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed during the white paper phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Turbulent flow over soft fouling & compliant surfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase fundamental knowledge of the triadic interactions between turbulent boundary layer flow, soft fouling biology and compliant surfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on interactions that affect drag, flow noise, fouling/adherence and coating performance under high Reynolds number flows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — influence of surface topology on fouling
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) influence of biotic and abiotic surface topology on fouling mechanisms, structures, and rates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study how topology at multiple scales affects settlement, attachment and growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — dependence on environment and surface properties
rubrics_metrics.description: (ii) dependence of fouling mechanisms and growth on environmental factors and material surface properties
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include environmental drivers and material property studies (e.g., hydrodynamics, chemistry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — biomechanical properties of soft fouling
rubrics_metrics.description: (iii) biomechanical properties of SF and BF
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize mechanical properties of fouling organisms and biofilms using in situ microscopy, gene expression tagging, and embedded sensors where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — interactions among TBL, fouling, wall vibrations
rubrics_metrics.description: (iv) interaction between the TBL flow, fouling organisms, flow-induced wall vibrations, and resultant impact on drag, flow noise, fouling and coating adhesion response
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate fluid-structure-biological coupling including potential lock-in effects and impact on coating adhesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — suggested model systems and techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Research can focus on a model system comprised of single organism cultures of BF and/or filamentous algae over rigid and elastomeric surfaces in high Re biofouling flow loops or channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Cellulophaga lytica, and Ulva linza; leverage advanced diagnostics (SPIV, TPIV, MIR facilities, interferometry, MTV/POV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — funding and team size (Topic 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards under this topic will not exceed an average of $1.5M/year for 5 years, supporting six faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions should be discussed with the topic chiefs during the white paper phase of the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: HBCU/MI participation incentive (Topic 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for Topic 21 are invited that include participation from eligible HBCUs/MIs; applications with an HBCU/MI MURI team member may be eligible for $1.5M in total additional funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is invited but not a requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Piezoceramics with Organized Macro-Symmetry (POMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop mechanistic understanding of the template grain growth process for achieving controlled macroscale symmetry and establish rational design strategies to efficiently explore compositional and crystallographic spaces for desired physical properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to enable prediction and validation of promising compositions via symmetry design aided by theoretical and computational approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — diffusion and transport in multi-element environment
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) diffusion and transport phenomena in a multi-element environment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study transport, grain boundary chemistry, and kinetics relevant to templated grain growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — phase stability and chemical compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) establishment of phase stability and chemical compatibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine thermodynamic and chemical constraints that govern templating and grain growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — seeding strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) seeding strategy including composition, morphology, symmetry, pattern, and associated crystal chemistry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate platelet seeding, template selection and patterning strategies to control macro-symmetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — in-situ characterization of grain growth
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) in-situ characterization of the template grain growth process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use advanced 3D microstructural characterization and in-situ experiments to observe growth dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — origin of dielectric and mechanical losses
rubrics_metrics.description: (5) origin of dielectric and mechanical losses under high electric field and high stresses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate loss mechanisms that limit performance under operational conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — computational material design techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: (6) computational techniques that facilitate material design and prediction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop computational tools for design and predictive capabilities across compositional/crystallographic spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — novel concepts for multiscale symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: (7) novel concepts for multiscale symmetry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore additive manufacturing and metamaterials approaches to create symmetry at multiple length scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — demonstration of transducer design
rubrics_metrics.description: (8) demonstration of unique transducer design using organized macro-symmetry concept
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide experimental demonstrations showing unique device-level functionality enabled by POMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — funding and team size (Topic 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting 5-7 faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chiefs during the white paper phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Measuring, modeling, manipulating variability in judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Gain a deepened understanding of measuring, modeling, and manipulating the variability in judgments and decision making, leading to experimentally validated techniques for identifying highly variable judgments and for measuring, modeling, and manipulating that variability to improve decision making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include tasks representative of military activities and scale methodologies to more complex decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — multidisciplinary expertise requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The envisioned research requires multidisciplinary expertise in organizational psychology, social and behavioral sciences, mathematics, computer science/AI, and human-computer interaction to design experiments, extract/analyze/interpret data, and create/validate predictive computational models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams should combine experimental, computational, and HCI expertise to address measurement, modeling and manipulation of variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — minimally intrusive measurement techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are sought for minimally intrusive techniques to measure decision making noise in cases where variability is undesirable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques should capture decisions and performance in naturalistic settings without altering behavior significantly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — predictive computational modeling of noise
rubrics_metrics.description: Create and empirically validate computational models of the mechanisms underlying noise generation in decision making
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models should predict how variability is modulated and its impact on decision-making processes and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — techniques and experimental manipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose and experimentally test manipulations of variability within socio-technical systems
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop interventions, experimental conditions and hypotheses for manipulating variability to improve performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration — evaluation and generalization of models
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirically validated approaches for evaluating and generalizing the models across multiple use cases
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how models and manipulations generalize beyond initial tasks and scale to more complex decision contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive-proposal deliverable — identify candidates and capture data
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive proposals will develop and demonstrate methods of identifying candidates for highly variable decisions/judgements as well as capturing and quantifying activities, decisions, and performance in naturalistic settings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on identification, measurement fidelity, and real-world data capture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive-proposal deliverable — predictive modeling and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive proposals will develop and demonstrate predictive computational modeling of the processes underlying the modulation of variability in decisions and the impacts of this variability on decision making processes and performance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models should be predictive and tied to experimental validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive-proposal deliverable — techniques & hypotheses for manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive proposals will develop and demonstrate techniques, experimental conditions, and hypotheses for manipulating variability within socio-technical systems
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include causal, experimentally controlled manipulations to derive mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive-proposal deliverable — validated evaluation & generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive proposals will develop and demonstrate empirically validated approaches for evaluating and generalizing the models across multiple use cases
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate cross-domain generalization and robustness.
